section: Cultural and Educational Rights - Articles 29-30; the right to property and the 44th Amendment

accepted.s: For determining whether a group is a linguistic minority in a State, which one of the following is the appropriate unit of reference?
o: The Union Territory having the largest population of that language
accepted.x: The State is the unit for determining a linguistic minority. The test also considers numerical inferiority, non-dominant status and distinct identity.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional unit of comparison rather than the size of the group at the national level.

accepted.s: Which of the following combination of criteria is relevant for determining a linguistic minority?
o: Numerical inferiority, non-dominant status in the State and distinct identity
Religious affiliation, urban residence and educational backwardness
Numerical superiority, political dominance and common occupation
District-level residence, income status and electoral representation
accepted.x: Determination involves numerical inferiority, non-dominant status in the State and a distinct linguistic identity.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete set of linked criteria instead of relying on numerical strength alone.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding linguistic minorities in India:
1. The Constitution expressly defines the expression “linguistic minority”.
2. The State is the unit for determining a linguistic minority.
3. Numerical inferiority and non-dominant status are relevant considerations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Constitution does not expressly define “linguistic minority”; therefore, statement 1 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement carrying an incorrect constitutional definition while retaining the two substantive tests.

accepted.s: The National Commission for Minorities is best described as a:
o: Judicial body established under the Protection of Civil Rights Act
Statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
Non-statutory advisory body created by executive resolution
accepted.x: The National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a statutory commission from a constitutional office and an executive body.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six religious minorities notified for the purposes of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Linguistic minorities as a general category
accepted.x: The six notified religious minorities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. “Linguistic minorities” is not one of the six notified religious categories.
accepted.tq: Find the category that does not belong to the notified religious-minority list.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
 a. Article 347
 b. Article 350
 c. Article 350A
 d. Article 350B

List-II (Provision)
 i. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
 ii. Representation for grievances in any language used in the Union or a State
 iii. Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
 iv. Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for linguistic-minority children

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State; Article 350 concerns language for grievances; Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction; and Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Article–provision pair and eliminate codes that disturb the remaining relationships.

accepted.s: Under Article 347 of the Constitution, the President may recognise:
o: Any foreign language demanded by a linguistic minority
A language spoken by a substantial part of the population of a State
Only the language spoken by the majority of the State
Only the official language of the Union for use in a State
accepted.x: Article 347 empowers the President to recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of the population of a State.
accepted.tq: Test the precise constitutional trigger and avoid extreme words such as “only”.

accepted.s: A person submits a representation for the redress of a grievance in a language used in the Union or in the State. Which constitutional provision is directly relevant?
accepted.x: Article 350 provides for representation for the redress of grievances in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State.
accepted.tq: Match the practical administrative situation with the exact Article dealing with grievances.

accepted.s: The constitutional provision relating to instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for children belonging to linguistic minority groups is:
accepted.x: Article 350A deals with facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely numbered Articles 350, 350A and 350B by their functions.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Article 350B is correct?
o: It creates the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
It enables the President to recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of a State.
It permits grievances to be submitted only in the official language of the Union.
It guarantees mother-tongue instruction in all stages of education.
accepted.x: Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, also known as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
accepted.tq: Separate the office-creating provision from the neighbouring language-related safeguards.

accepted.s: A publication prints the constitutional clause concerning mother-tongue instruction for linguistic-minority children as Article 360A. What is the correct constitutional Article?
accepted.x: The mother-tongue instruction clause is contained in Article 350A. Article 360A is a misprint in the cited publication.
accepted.tq: Prefer the exact constitutional provision over a look-alike Article number.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 31B — Laws concerning acquisition of estates and agrarian reform
Article 31A — Acts placed in the Ninth Schedule
Article 31C — Laws implementing Article 39(b) and Article 39(c)
Article 350A — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
accepted.x: Article 31C protects laws implementing Article 39(b) and 39(c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19, subject to the constitutional and judicial limitations. Article 31A concerns estate acquisition and agrarian reform, Article 31B concerns Ninth Schedule laws, and Article 350B creates the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
accepted.tq: Check each Article against its precise subject and identify the only correctly matched pair.

accepted.s: Article 31C was inserted by the:
accepted.x: Article 31C was inserted by the Twenty-Fifth Amendment Act, 1971 to protect laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19.
accepted.tq: Separate the amendment associated with Article 31C from the First Amendment associated with Articles 31A and 31B.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Ninth Schedule is correct?
o: It contains only laws implementing Article 39(b) and Article 39(c).
It contains fewer than 50 entries and enjoys complete immunity from judicial review.
It has grown to more than 280 entries, but inclusion does not confer blanket immunity from judicial review.
It has grown to more than 280 entries, and its contents have no constitutional relationship with Fundamental Rights.
accepted.x: The Ninth Schedule has grown to more than 280 entries, but inclusion does not provide blanket immunity from judicial review, particularly after the decisions in Waman Rao and I.R. Coelho.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim of complete immunity and combine the numerical fact with the judicial limitation.

accepted.s: In Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981), the Supreme Court held that laws added to the Ninth Schedule after which date could be tested against the basic structure doctrine?
accepted.x: Waman Rao treated laws added to the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 as open to challenge on the basis of the basic structure doctrine.
accepted.tq: Test the decisive cut-off date associated with the judicial review of Ninth Schedule entries.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the effect of the decision in I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007)?
o: Only laws enacted before 1973 may be challenged under Article 31B.
Ninth Schedule entries made after 1973 may be invalidated if they damage the essence of Articles 14, 19 or 21.
Every Ninth Schedule law is permanently immune from judicial review.
accepted.x: I.R. Coelho held that there is no blanket immunity for post-1973 Ninth Schedule entries; they can be invalidated if they damage the essence of Articles 14, 19 or 21.
accepted.tq: Identify the judicial qualification that defeats an absolute immunity statement.

accepted.s: The year 2026 marked how many years of the First Amendment to the Constitution?
accepted.x: The First Amendment was enacted in 1951, making 2026 its 75th anniversary. It received the assent of President Rajendra Prasad.
accepted.tq: Calculate the anniversary from the amendment year and distinguish it from later constitutional amendments.

accepted.s:
Which of the following were associated with the First Amendment Act, 1951?
1. Insertion of Article 15(4)
2. Insertion of Articles 31A and 31B
3. Addition of public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement as grounds under Article 19(2)
4. Insertion of Article 31C
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The First Amendment added Article 15(4), Articles 31A and 31B, and the stated grounds under Article 19(2). Article 31C was inserted by the Twenty-Fifth Amendment Act, 1971.
accepted.tq: Separate provisions belonging to the First Amendment from the closely related provision inserted by the Twenty-Fifth Amendment.

accepted.s: Which recent development was reported as creating concern regarding the Kannada linguistic minority in Kasaragod?
o: A central notification replacing all State languages with Hindi
A Malayalam language Bill in Kerala receiving assent in March 2026
A judicial decision removing the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
accepted.x: The Kerala Malayalam Bhasha Bill received assent in March 2026 and was contested on the ground that it could harm the Kannada linguistic minority in Kasaragod.
accepted.tq: Connect the current-affairs development with the precise linguistic-minority issue involved.

accepted.s: Which one of the following concerns has been raised in debates relating to minority educational institutions?
o: The abolition of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
A constitutional prohibition on minority-run schools receiving any public assistance
A complete prohibition on mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
Misuse of minority status to avoid obligations under the Right to Education framework
accepted.x: A criticism in the debate is that minority status may sometimes be misused to escape obligations under the Right to Education framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated criticism without converting it into an absolute constitutional prohibition.

accepted.s: The criticism that amendments to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act may threaten minority-run civil society organisations relates to:
o: The appointment of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities
FCRA amendments and their effect on minority-run civil society
Article 347 and recognition of State languages
accepted.x: The stated concern is that FCRA amendments may pose a threat to minority-run civil society organisations.
accepted.tq: Match the policy measure with the specific civil-society concern rather than a constitutional language provision.

accepted.s: In GGR Housing v. State, the Andhra Pradesh High Court emphasised:
o: Strict statutory due process in land acquisition under Article 300A
The abolition of Article 300A as a legal right
The conversion of the right to property into a Fundamental Right
The exclusion of land acquisition from judicial review
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh High Court insisted on strict statutory due process in land acquisition under Article 300A. Article 300A protects the right to property as a legal constitutional right.
accepted.tq: Apply the case principle to the constitutional protection governing deprivation of property.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh minority cell fast-tracked direct benefit transfer of post-matric scholarships subject to an income ceiling of:
accepted.x: The reported post-matric scholarship initiative applied an income ceiling of Rs 2.5 lakh and used direct benefit transfer.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise eligibility ceiling and distinguish it from nearby round-number distractors.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 31C — Protection of laws relating to acquisition of estates from Articles 14 and 19
Article 350B — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 350A — Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
Article 347 — Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
accepted.x: Article 31C protects laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19. Protection for laws relating to acquisition of estates and agrarian reform is associated with Article 31A.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped subject between the neighbouring provisions of Articles 31A and 31C.
